name: mos-substrate-firewall
description: MOS v2.0 substrate boundary rules (W0-B / BOOT-003). Machine-readable authority for harness/mos-boundary-check.mjs. Mirrors spec/mos-architecture-policy-v2.0.yaml (forbidDeepImports, forbidConcreteEngineImportsFromDomain, forbidProviderCallsOutsideIntegration) and the ZCode substrate firewall section of docs/architecture/ZCODE-SUBSTRATE-INVENTORY-v1.md.

rules.description: MOS domain packages (packages/mos-*) may import ONLY: relative paths within their own package, @mos/* workspace packages, and node builtins (node: prefixed form or bare builtin name). Any @zcode/* import in a MOS domain package is a violation (kind zcode-import); any other non-relative import is a violation (kind disallowed-import).

ONLY packages/zcode-substrate-adapters/src/adapters/** may import @zcode/*. Inside that root, only the exact package-entry names in zcodeEntryAllowlist are allowed — deep imports (e.g. @zcode/rpc/dist/internal) and non-allowlisted entries (e.g. @zcode/web) are violations (kind non-allowlisted-entry). Any @zcode/* import outside the adapters root is a violation (kind outside-adapter-root). Files in MOS domain packages additionally violate MOS-DOMAIN-IMPORT-BOUNDARY (dual reporting is intentional: each rule has its own remediation).

No MOS-managed package (packages/mos-* or packages/zcode-substrate-adapters) may import engine/provider SDKs. Matching is by package root: exact match for bare names (openai, ffmpeg, ...), scope-prefix match for scoped names (@google/*, @aws-sdk/*). Engines are reached through capability contract -> engine registry -> engine adapter -> sandbox, never imported directly (spec/mos-architecture-policy-v2.0.yaml forbidConcreteEngineImportsFromDomain).

Port contract files (any path containing the segment sequence src/ports/) never import @zcode/* — only adapters may. Port files must stay MOS-owned and substrate-free so the contracts can be extracted/promoted (e.g. into @mos/contracts) without untangling substrate types.
